newsitem.title: FRANCE: Carnage, kidnapping in Algeria, upto 110 dead-papers.
newsitem.headline: Carnage, kidnapping in Algeria, upto 110 dead-papers.

text.p: In a series of savage raids, Moslem rebels killed between 75 and 110 civilians in Algeria, cutting the throats of children and dragging off screaming young girls, Algerian newspapers said on Tuesday.

The attacks in two provinces were carried out just hours after President Liamine Zeroual on Sunday vowed that rebels, who have killed more than 700 people in two months, would be implacably hunted down for crimes which he said "defy human understanding".
Just before midnight on Sunday, rebels attacked two family homes in Amroussa village, Blida province, some 50 km (30 miles) south of the Algerian capital, Le Matin newspaper said.
"Nineteen members of the Zemim family, including a three-month-old baby, were decapitated by axes.

"Two young girls, members of the same family, miraculously escaped the massacre. The first was wounded while the second, who had been kidnapped with her three sisters, was able to flee her abductors..." the paper said.
It said one of the young girls dragged away was found next day, her throat slit. "The seven other victims came from the Hachou family whose house is 20 metres from the Zemim home."
El Watan, well informed on security issues, said the attackers split into two groups, one keeping the local communal guard blocked in its station while the others carried out the killings.
"The screams of the women and children at no time made the assassins hesitate...they burst into laughter each time a neck was sliced," it said, quoting witnesses.
El Watan said that among the dead were eight children aged between 40 days and eight years.

"One baby, aged two months, was pulled from the arms of its mother who begged the terrorists to kill her before killing her child. The baby was decapitated, then burnt before the eyes of its parents...," the paper said.
One "terrorist" told three young girls: "You will serve the emir (gang leader). He is waiting for you."
Despite their cries and efforts to escape, they were taken. "And God alone knows what fate these assassins reserve for them."
El Watan said that around 40 more people were assassinated in two mountain villages at the weekend in Ain Defla province. It named them as Mzaourou and Oued El-Had, in Arib district.
Le Matin put the toll in Ain Defla at 76, saying killings took place overnight Sunday-Monday in the villages of Oued El Ilad, Sidi M'Hjand Ameziane and Erradjm.
Eight more people died and seven were wounded at a fake road block at Hammam Melouane, in Blida province, Le Matin added.

The latest killings bring to at least 250 the toll among civilians in the past 10 days and take to more than 1,000 the number of people reported killed since June 5, when Algeria held a general election which officials hoped would see a start to ending the near six-year-old conflict.
Officials blame the killings on Moslem rebels. At first the killers were described as FIS hardliners, then came other factions, with the Armed Islamic Group (GIA) seen as the most ruthless.
About 60,000 people have been killed since violence erupted after the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election dominated by the fundamentalist Islamic Salvation Front (FIS).
Algeria is preparing to hold local elections on October 23, which Zeroual said on Sunday would take it to "cross the final phase of re-establishing its institutional stability".
Until Zeroual's remarks, the authorities had not commented on the surge in violence which Zeroual termed a "phenomenon which has cruelly plunged the Algerian family into mourning."

"Abject and barbarous crime, like that which happens on the eve of each determining event in the nation's future, has again shown itself in acts which defy human understanding and challenge the sacred character of human life," the president said.
